name: Sierra Space
desc: Defense-tech space company building the Dream Chaser spaceplane, satellites, spacecraft subsystems and commercial space station modules.
capacity_detail: Series C USD 550M (Mar 2026) at USD 8bn post-money valuation; over USD 2bn raised since 2021
markets: United States national security, NASA and civil customers plus commercial space station and cargo services to low Earth orbit

signals.raise: USD 550M Series C at USD 8bn valuation (Mar 2026; https://www.sierraspace.com/press-releases/sierra-space-closes-550-million-in-series-c-round-with-a-valuation-of-8-billion/)

rationale: Well-funded, engineering-led brand seeking government and commercial customers; F1 technology storytelling suits Dream Chaser and its recruiting needs.

name: Vast
desc: Privately held company building the Haven commercial space stations, aiming to replace the International Space Station around 2030.
capacity_detail: USD 500M raised Mar 2026 (USD 300M equity + USD 200M debt); company says over USD 1bn private capital invested
markets: NASA and US government, private astronaut missions, microgravity research customers; investors include Qatar Investment Authority, Mitsui and Nikon

signals.raise: USD 300M equity and USD 200M debt led by Balerion Space Ventures (Mar 2026; https://www.vastspace.com/updates/vast-secures-500m-in-funding-to-accelerate-production-of-haven-space-stations)

rationale: Consumer-facing human spaceflight brand selling private astronaut missions to wealthy individuals and nations, an audience F1 hospitality reaches directly.

name: Apex Space
desc: Manufactures productized, configurable satellite bus platforms at industrial scale for commercial and US government constellations.
capacity_detail: Over USD 200M growth funding at USD 2.3bn valuation (Jun 2026), led by Glade Brook Capital Partners
markets: Commercial and US government satellite customers, including Space Force missile-defence work with Northrop Grumman, from its Los Angeles factory
rationale: High-rate manufacturing story parallels F1 engineering; F1 platform helps recruit engineers and signal scale to constellation buyers.

name: SpaceSail
desc: Shanghai Spacecom Satellite Technology builds and operates the Qianfan low Earth orbit satellite internet constellation rivalling Starlink.
capacity_detail: Raised nearly CNY 7bn (USD 1.94bn) in Aug 2026 at a valuation of about CNY 50.1bn; state SOE Structural Adjustment Fund consortium took 11.5%
markets: China, Brazil (licence for up to 324 satellites), talks in Thailand and Malaysia, maritime internet tests in Hong Kong

signals.raise: Nearly CNY 7bn round at about CNY 50.1bn valuation (Aug 2026; https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-19/spacecom-raises-194-billion-in-bet-on-chinas-starlink-rival-102475501.html)
signals.regions: Brazil regulator approved Qianfan to operate up to 324 satellites (Aug 2026; https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-19/spacecom-raises-194-billion-in-bet-on-chinas-starlink-rival-102475501.html)

rationale: Starlink challenger expanding into Brazil and Southeast Asia needs global consumer brand awareness; F1 races in those markets offer reach.

name: Space Pioneer
desc: Beijing Tianbing Technology develops reusable Tianlong rockets and Tianhuo liquid engines for satellite internet and space station resupply launches.
capacity_detail: Series C (Jul 2023) brought total raised to around USD 414M, per Wikipedia
markets: Chinese national satellite internet constellations and CNSA Tiangong cargo resupply launch market
rationale: Launch provider competing for megaconstellation contracts; F1 sponsorship in China could raise its profile with commercial satellite customers.

name: Neo Space Group
desc: PIF-owned Saudi group covering satellite communications, earth observation, satellite navigation and IoT, plus a space venture fund.
capacity_detail: Wholly owned PIF company launched May 2024 to be a national champion and leading commercial player in the global satellite sector
markets: Saudi Arabia, with plans to offer satellite and space solutions internationally and invest in overseas assets
rationale: PIF portfolio brands (Aramco, STC, Saudi Arabian GP) already use F1; NSG seeks global commercial profile for Saudi space ambitions.

name: GMV
desc: Spanish privately owned technology group providing space ground systems, satellite navigation, defence, transport and cybersecurity solutions.
capacity_detail: Total income EUR 510.25M in 2025, EBITDA EUR 43.65M
markets: Offices in 12 countries and clients in nearly 80, serving space agencies, defence, transport, health and finance
rationale: Spain's motorsport boom and GMV's automotive and navigation businesses fit F1 B2B hospitality and engineering-talent recruitment goals.

name: Marlink
desc: Provides managed satellite, LEO, terrestrial and 5G connectivity plus cybersecurity for shipping, energy, cruise and government users.
capacity_detail: Annual revenue USD 800M stated by the company (year not given)
markets: Offices in 30+ countries, 15,000 vessels managed, serving shipping, energy, cruise, defence and humanitarian sectors
rationale: B2B connectivity brand selling to global shipping and energy firms; F1 hospitality and connectivity storytelling fit its enterprise sales.

name: Beyond Gravity
desc: Swiss space supplier making launcher structures, satellite dispensers and satellite components, owned by the Swiss Confederation.
capacity_detail: RUAG International (Beyond Gravity) net sales CHF 412.0M in 2025 (CHF 494.9M in 2024)
markets: Sites in Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, Portugal, United States and Finland supplying launcher and satellite makers worldwide
rationale: Precision-engineering supplier with a new brand; F1 engineering association could raise visibility with global launch and satellite primes.
